description: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is the only global international organization dealing with the rules of trade between nations. It facilitates trade agreements, provides a forum for trade negotiations, and settles trade disputes among member countries.

sections.title: Origin and Historical Background
sections.description: A brief history of the creation of the WTO and its predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).

historical_events.significance: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) was signed by 23 countries to promote international trade by reducing tariffs and trade barriers.
This was the 8th and largest round of GATT negotiations, which successfully laid out the framework for creating the WTO.
Signed by 123 nations in Marrakesh, Morocco, this agreement officially approved the creation of the World Trade Organization.
The WTO officially replaced GATT and commenced operations as the global body regulating international trade.

important_facts.fact: The headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO) is located in Geneva, Switzerland.
Unlike the World Bank or IMF, the WTO is NOT a specialized agency of the United Nations (UN); it is an independent global organization.

sections.title: Basic Principles of WTO
sections.description: The fundamental trading principles of the WTO designed to ensure a fair, transparent, and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system.

key_concepts.explanation: The principle of non-discrimination between trading partners. If a country grants a special favor (like a lower customs duty) to one partner, it must extend the same concession to all other WTO members.

The principle of giving others the same treatment as one's own nationals. Imported and domestically produced goods, services, and intellectual property must be treated equally once foreign goods have entered the domestic market.

sections.title: Major Agreements of WTO
sections.description: Various multilateral agreements under the WTO covering trade in goods, services, and intellectual property.

key_concepts.concept: TRIPS (Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights)
key_concepts.explanation: Sets minimum standards for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights, including patents, copyrights, industrial designs, and geographical indications (GI).
Restricts investment measures that limit or distort trade. For example, it prohibits imposing 'local content requirements' on foreign investors.
Aims to establish a fair and market-oriented agricultural trading system. It rests on three main pillars: Market Access, Domestic Support (subsidies), and Export Subsidies.

key_concepts.concept: GATS (General Agreement on Trade in Services)
key_concepts.explanation: The first and only multilateral agreement covering international trade in the service sector, such as banking, telecommunications, IT, and tourism.

sections.title: Agricultural Subsidy Boxes (Under AoA)
sections.description: Under the Agreement on Agriculture (AoA), domestic support or agricultural subsidies are categorized into 'boxes' based on their trade-distorting effects.

key_concepts.explanation: Includes all domestic subsidies that directly distort production and trade, such as Minimum Support Price (MSP) or fertilizer subsidies. Under WTO rules, these must be reduced over time.

Subsidies that do not distort trade, or cause minimal distortion. These include funding for agricultural research, environmental protection, and disaster relief. There is no monetary limit on Green Box subsidies.
Often described as the 'Amber Box with conditions'. It includes trade-distorting subsidies that are tied to programs requiring farmers to limit their production levels to prevent oversupply.

sections.title: Trade Agreements and Economic Integration
sections.description: Different levels of bilateral and regional economic cooperation and integration between countries.

key_concepts.explanation: An agreement between two or more countries where they agree to substantially reduce or eliminate customs duties and trade barriers on most products traded between them.
A form of economic integration which is an FTA with a common external tariff. Member countries adopt uniform tariffs against imports from non-member countries.
More comprehensive than an FTA, a CEPA covers not just trade in goods, but also trade in services, investments, intellectual property, and other areas of economic cooperation.

sections.title: Major Regional Trade Associations
sections.description: Prominent regional free trade agreements and economic blocs around the world.

key_associations.extra_info: A free trade agreement that came into force in 2006 among seven South Asian nations: India, Pakistan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Bhutan, and the Maldives.
It is the world's largest trade agreement among 15 Asia-Pacific nations. India formally opted out of the RCEP negotiations in 2019.
The new, upgraded version of the older NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement), which officially came into force in 2020.
